records.normalizedEnglish: Author says muscle-control practice should be learned before subsequent exercises; full-control/mastery wording provides no numeric assessment gate. Body/mind/will and thought-vibration theory are historical.

Relaxed comfortable sitting: five minutes, then ten, then fifteen when easy. No rigid or tense sitting, no overfatigue. Little-and-often advice has no count; rest-cure assertion is historical, not treatment.
records.originalRussian: Вы не должны переутомлять себя какъ этимъ, такъ и какимъ-либо другимъ упражненіемъ.

records.normalizedEnglish: Sit upright, prescribed head/chin/shoulders; right arm sideways at shoulder level, look toward fingertips, palm down; one minute each side, then two, three and eventually five.
Brim-full small water glass held with fingers, arm in front, observe water movement; one minute gradually to five limit, alternate hands. No intermediate increments specified.

Avoid muscular tension at rest; author urges composed manners and suppressing tapping, leg movement, rocking, nail/lip biting, tongue noises, blinking, twitching and startle. These directives are historical, not guided suppression of natural movement or neurodivergent regulation.

Table-supported hands, fists palm-up/thumb across fingers; move thumb, unfold fingers in order, reverse from little finger, left hand. Five per session, later ten, sustained attention. Fatigue/persistence claims preserved historically; guided stops for discomfort.
Interlace fingers with thumbs free, slowly circle one thumb around the other, attend to tips; no time/count.
Right hand on knee, fist except extended index; move index slowly side to side, attend tip; no time/count.
Simple ordinary monotonous motions with attention on moving part; strict-teacher/pupil metaphor and demands not to drift are historical. No invented numbered variant or objective concentration score.

Choose ordinary uninteresting object such as pencil; five minutes look, turn, inspect and consider use/materials/manufacture, imagine self and pencil alone. Continue ordinary-object requirement; not sharpening.
Practice variants using everyday objects and revisit earlier lessons; author claims self-control grants control over others. No such interpersonal domination result is promised or guided.
